name: Ray Peat diet

lead: The Ray Peat diet is built around milk, fruit and juice, root vegetables, eggs, shellfish and saturated fats while avoiding polyunsaturated fats. Followers aim for a leaner, more energetic look through a higher metabolic rate and better hormone balance.

Proponents say lowering PUFA intake and eating sugar- and dairy-rich foods supports thyroid function and metabolic rate and lowers estrogen. These ideas come from Raymond Peat's writings; no clinical trials of the diet were found, and forum discussion mixes enthusiastic reports with scepticism.

paras: People build meals around milk, cheese, fruit, orange juice, eggs, shellfish and gelatin or collagen, cook with butter or coconut oil, and avoid seed oils, nuts and fatty fish. It is followed as an ongoing eating pattern, with users reporting changes over weeks.
No harms were documented in the sources reviewed. Users in forums mention hormone-related side effects anecdotally, and extreme claims such as height gain are not supported by published research.

social.title: Ray Peat Diet: What Is It, and Does It Work?

angle.text: Followers eat milk, fruit, juice and saturated fats to raise metabolism and correct hormone balance, aiming for a leaner, healthier look. The approach comes from Peat's writings and user reports; no trials of the diet were found.

lead: The Ray Peat diet is an eating pattern inspired by the writings of Raymond Peat, an American author on nutrition and physiology. Followers describe it as "pro-metabolic" and aimed at correcting hormonal imbalances and raising metabolic rate. Typical elements are milk, cheese, fruit and fruit juice, root vegetables, eggs, shellfish, muscle and organ meats, collagen, and saturated fats such as butter and coconut oil, while polyunsaturated fats are avoided.

On looksmax.org the diet is discussed alongside claims about hormones, thyroid function and even height. No clinical trials of the diet were found in the sources reviewed, and the wiki records community claims as claims.
infobox: Dairy, fruit and juice, root vegetables, eggs, shellfish
Polyunsaturated fats (nuts, seeds, seed oils, fatty fish)

paras: As summarised in a looksmax.org post quoting a hospital dietitian, the diet emphasises healthy saturated fats, a heavy share of dairy, abundant fresh fruit and juice, root vegetables, animal protein and collagen. Followers cite the instability of PUFAs to explain why they are excluded.
Community resource threads collect Peat's writings on metabolic rate and hormones, sodium and water retention, and nicotine.

Forum members discuss the diet for hormones, skin and metabolism. One thread asserted that Peat gained roughly an inch in height in his 40s with DHEA supplementation; a reply expressed scepticism, noting that Peat made many other claims of rapid recovery. Another thread pairs Peat's approach with raw animal-food diets.
Community opinion is divided; thread titles include both enthusiastic and critical reactions.
